confirmed_facts.claim: SBI Holdings and SMBC Group signed a capital/business alliance on October 30, 2026 to jointly study stablecoin-based financial services. SMBC Group agreed to take a 5% equity stake in SBI Startale Marketing, the SBI-Startale JV promoting JPYSC. The investment amount and production use cases are not disclosed.

SBI's SBI-Sygnum-Azimut Digital Asset Opportunity Fund decided to invest in Hong Kong-based PhotonPay; the investment amount is undisclosed. SBI reports PhotonPay has 60+ currencies, 100+ remittance routes, 33 payment/financial licences, 200+ countries served, 4.4M cards issued over the prior 12 months, and USD65B annualized total payment volume as of August 2026. The USD65B is total platform volume across fiat and stablecoin rails, not stablecoin-only volume.

PhotonPay conducted a Mastercard AI-agent payment proof-of-concept in May 2026 using per-transaction card tokens. This is a PhotonPay-Mastercard PoC, not evidence of an SBI-Mastercard production payment route or XRP settlement.

SBI and Startale joined Open Standard on October 16, 2026. The alliance announcement names Visa, Stripe, Mastercard, BlackRock and Coinbase among 140+ participating companies and reports more than 200 institutions/fintechs/businesses signed up. SBI/Startale will explore a pilot connecting JPYSC and OUSD; the announcement explicitly says this is exploration, not a commercial service or production settlement.

SBI Holdings, Startale and BlackRock Financial Management/BlackRock Japan signed an October 27 MOU to explore a digital-asset ecosystem connecting a tokenized money-market fund and JPYSC across technology, business/distribution and regulatory/market preparation. The specific fund/token, chain, balances and production timetable are not disclosed.

As of September 7, 2026, JPYSC issuance was approximately JPY20.1B. SBI Shinsei Trust Bank had begun investing JPY10B of trust backing assets in short-term Japanese government bonds under the amended Payment Services Act. SBI VC Trade reported approximately JPY6.9B of JPYSC lending applications; this is applications, not confirmed accepted or outstanding loans.

JPYSC launched June 24, 2026 initially for use only inside SBI VC Trade accounts. External-wallet transfers/deposits/withdrawals were not enabled; public-chain circulation was conditional on legal/tax treatment and supervisory confirmation.
SBI announced JPYSC lending from July 16, 2026 with an initial annualized offer of 3%. This is a product offer, not realized yield or proof of accepted loan balances.
SBI invested approximately USD50M in Startale Group in March 2026 and planned to make it an equity-method affiliate. This is strategic equity capital, not JPYSC reserve capital or XRP purchases.

SBI separately has a 50/50 Circle SBI Japan KK JV and distributes Ripple RLUSD through SBI VC Trade. VCTRADE currently lists USDC and RLUSD on Ethereum; RLUSD's dedicated page says XRPL support is planned, not live.
SBIC East Japan remains a separate Japanese SME investment corporation; it is not SBI Holdings or the SBI-Startale JPYSC JV.

SBI VC Trade's current VCTRADE network-support FAQ lists native XRP on the XRP Ledger, USDC on Ethereum, RLUSD on Ethereum, and JPYSC as unsupported for deposits and withdrawals. This is a venue-specific operational route matrix, not a statement about all SBI affiliates or third-party venues.

SBI VC Trade's USDC deposit FAQ accepts USDC only when sent over Ethereum and states a 1 million JPY-equivalent per-deposit limit. The FAQ warns that USDC sent over BNB Smart Chain, Arbitrum or other unsupported networks will not be credited or recoverable.

Circle's USDC is natively available on XRPL, and Ripple/Circle announced the XRPL deployment. SBI VC Trade's own current route matrix nevertheless lists USDC on Ethereum only. Issuer-level native deployment therefore does not equal SBI VC Trade XRPL deposit/withdrawal support.

Ripple and SBI launched RLUSD in Japan through SBI VC Trade in June 2026. SBI's product page and current network FAQ list Ethereum as the live VCTRADE network; the dedicated product page describes XRP Ledger support as planned rather than live.

inferences: SBI is assembling a multi-rail APAC digital-finance network spanning USDC, RLUSD, JPYSC, a proposed OUSD connection, tokenized money-market funds, fiat/stablecoin cross-border payments and institutional banking partners.
The SMBC 5% investment in SBI Startale Marketing is a direct capital relationship into the JPYSC commercialization vehicle, not a direct investment in XRP, Ripple, Circle or JPYSC reserves.

SBI's Open Standard participation creates a shared consortium relationship with Coinbase and Mastercard, but not proof of a bilateral commercial agreement, a direct Coinbase-SBI integration or any XRP settlement.

PhotonPay gives SBI exposure to a fiat/stablecoin payment platform with Mastercard agentic-payment experimentation. Its USD65B annualized volume is all-rail platform volume; stablecoin-specific volume and XRP usage are unknown.
JPYSC's JPY10B short-term JGB investment is a real reserve-allocation change and an actual-capital/collateralization observation. It does not create XRP demand.

JPYSC's account-only launch means the reported issuance and lending activity are not public-chain XRPL activity. The planned Open Standard and BlackRock integrations remain exploratory until external transfers and production settlement are observed.

The network's broad partner list includes Coinbase, Mastercard and BlackRock but does not identify Circle or Ripple as Open Standard founding partners; absence from this announcement is not proof of non-membership.

inferences.claim: At the SBI VC Trade VCTRADE deposit/withdrawal layer, native XRP is routable on XRPL while the two USD stablecoins distributed by the venue (USDC and RLUSD) are currently Ethereum-only and JPYSC is not transferable. This separates the venue's native XRP route from its stablecoin transfer routes.

competing_hypotheses.claim: SBI is building a multi-issuer, multi-currency APAC settlement and tokenized-asset ecosystem rather than an XRP-exclusive strategy.
competing_hypotheses.counterevidence: Most connections are MOU, investment, pilot or product-announcement stage; executed cross-network volumes and commercial economics are not disclosed.

competing_hypotheses.claim: JPYSC-OUSD interoperability could create yen-dollar on-chain liquidity and tokenized-asset settlement routes.
competing_hypotheses.counterevidence: JPYSC remains account-only with no external wallet transfers; Open Standard connection is pilot exploration; BlackRock arrangement is an MOU; no production transactions or launch date.

competing_hypotheses.claim: SBI's Open Standard membership establishes a direct commercial integration with Coinbase.
competing_hypotheses.counterevidence: The source establishes shared alliance membership and a JPYSC-OUSD pilot exploration; it does not disclose a bilateral contract, Coinbase integration workstream or XRP route.

competing_hypotheses.claim: PhotonPay's USD65B annualized TPV creates meaningful XRP demand through stablecoin payments.
competing_hypotheses.counterevidence: USD65B covers all fiat and stablecoin payment rails; stablecoin share, supported chains, XRP usage, liquidity-provider routes and executed XRP purchases are undisclosed.

competing_hypotheses.claim: JPYSC's short-term JGB reserve investment creates a collateral relationship with XRP.
competing_hypotheses.counterevidence: The JGBs back JPYSC trust assets; no XRP collateral or XRPL route is disclosed. Reserve assets and XRP collateral are distinct.

competing_hypotheses.claim: SBI VC Trade's current direct stablecoin deposit/withdrawal routes do not connect USDC or RLUSD to XRPL, even though Circle USDC and Ripple RLUSD are deployed on XRPL elsewhere.
competing_hypotheses.counterevidence: This is limited to SBI VC Trade's VCTRADE route matrix. Other SBI affiliates, Circle Mint, Ripple services, third-party exchanges, bridges and other XRPL gateways may provide separate routes.

competing_hypotheses.claim: VCTRADE can support native XRP deposits/withdrawals on XRPL while USDC/RLUSD transfers remain Ethereum-only and JPYSC transfers remain disabled.
competing_hypotheses.counterevidence: The FAQ does not disclose internal trading pairs, conversion paths, customer balances, liquidity depth or actual cross-asset settlement volume.

data_quality_correction.issue: The same source ID had been assigned to two different primary documents: SBI's October 27 announcement and Startale's own announcement.
data_quality_correction.correction: The Startale document now has the distinct source ID SRC-STARTALE-BLACKROCK-JPYSC-TOKENIZED-MMF-MOU-20261027. Both documents remain separately represented and the MOU relationship cites both.
data_quality_correction.source_independence_caveat: Both sources are counterparties to the same MOU. They independently publish the announcement but do not independently verify production execution, fund issuance, settlement or XRP use.

route_matrix.scope_limit: VCTRADE only; not all SBI Group affiliates or external venues.
